overview: Confidential file: Osaka Syosen Kaisya's Brazil Maru captain refused to carry Mutter and Leverman from Buenos Aires despite valid visas and paid fares, while previously-rejected passengers were accepted; the matter, tied to unclear belligerent-national policy, circulated to State, naval, and military intelligence.

subfiles.title: Confidential filing sheet for decimal file 894.856/1
subfiles.about: A filing marker identifies the material as confidential and assigns it decimal number 894.856/1.
subfiles.summary: Confidential filing sheet bears only the decimal number 894.856/1, marking the start of the substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Air-mail instruction No. 671 on passengers refused by the Brazil Maru
subfiles.about: The Secretary of State confidentially relays intelligence about the Brazil Maru captain’s refusal to carry Paul Mutter and W. Leverman.
subfiles.summary: Instruction quotes a report that Brazil Maru's captain refused Mutter and Leverman passage despite valid visas and paid fares, while previously rejected passengers were accepted, amid unclear Japanese policy on belligerent nationals.

subfiles.title: Government-agency letter to Berle concerning Brazil Maru passengers
subfiles.about: The source letter reports confidential information about Japanese acceptance and rejection of passengers and distributes it to State, naval, and military intelligence officials.
subfiles.summary: Letter to Berle confirms no written Japanese policy change on belligerent-national passengers, though visas were still issued to military-age men, signed by Hoover (misread in OCR) and copied to Naval and Army intelligence.

interest: Shows a 1941 Japanese line refusing passage to two visa-holding passengers, monitored by naval and military intelligence.
